Day 1
From Hotel: 12 min · 5 min → Museum Ludwig
1. Museum Ludwig
Top-tier modern and contemporary art museum with the largest Picasso collection outside Spain, plus outstanding Warhol and German Expressionism. Located beside the Cathedral, with over 3,600 artworks spanning Pop Art to Modernism.

2. Gross St. Martin
Romanesque church with a distinctive trefoil tower rising above the historic Altstadt, rebuilt after WWII from near-total destruction. One of Cologne's twelve medieval Romanesque basilicas, dating to the 12th century.

3. Cologne Cathedral
Gothic masterpiece with a 632-year construction history, twin spires dominating the Rhine skyline and the city’s defining landmark. A UNESCO World Heritage Site since 1996, housing the Shrine of the Three Kings reliquary.

4. Hohenzollern Bridge
Cologne’s iconic railway and pedestrian bridge across the Rhine, covered in millions of love padlocks attached to the fence railings by couples. Europe’s busiest rail bridge, connecting the Cathedral district to the Deutz bank.

Local Tastes
Kölsch
Cologne’s protected pale ale, served in 0.2L Kölner Stangen glasses by white-jacketed Köbes waiters who refill without asking until you cover the glass.
Früh am Dom · Peters Brauhaus · Malzmühle
Himmel un Ääd
Heaven and Earth — fried blood sausage with warm mashed potato and caramelized onions, a Rhineland staple found on every traditional menu.
Malzmühle · Brauhaus Sion
Halve Hahn
Half a Kölsch rye roll with aged Dutch Gouda and mustard — despite the name, no chicken is involved; the name refers to the bread shape.
Früh am Dom · Gasthaus Brungs
Reibekuchen
Crispy potato pancakes served with apple sauce or sour cream, sold at market stalls and traditional restaurants across the Old Town.
Alter Markt
Rheinischer Sauerbraten
Rhine-style pot roast marinated in vinegar and spices for several days, served with raisins, gingerbread sauce, and dark rye bread.
Gasthaus Brungs · Haxenhaus
Food Delivery
Lieferando
Foreign number: accepted.
Germany's dominant delivery platform and the default choice in Cologne; excellent coverage across Altstadt, Ehrenfeld, Nippes, and Sülz; by far the deepest local restaurant roster including independent kebab shops, Kölsch-food spots, and international cuisine.
lieferando.de
Uber Eats
Foreign number: accepted.
Good Cologne coverage with a mix of local restaurants and international chains; useful if you have an existing Uber account and want to avoid creating a second one — Lieferando typically has a broader local selection.
ubereats.com

Getting Around
Uber
Foreign number: accepted.
Good coverage across central Cologne and the main neighborhoods; reliable for evening trips to the Altstadt, Rheinauhafen, and beyond; works well alongside FREENOW — check both for availability during busy weekend nights.
uber.com
FREENOW
Foreign number: accepted.
Aggregates licensed taxis and private hire vehicles across Cologne; often more available than Uber during peak times; taxis dispatched through the app are metered so fares are predictable — particularly reliable near Cologne Hauptbahnhof and the Altstadt.
free-now.com

Worth Knowing

The Cathedral from Below and Above

Cross Hohenzollern Bridge at dusk. Position yourself on the south walkway facing west — the Cathedral’s twin spires catch the last light while their reflection moves across the Rhine below. This is the shot every photographer knows but the timing is everything.

Order Kölsch correctly. Place your coaster flat on the bar to signal you want another — cover the glass with the coaster when you’re done. Cologne’s white-jacketed Köbes waiters never ask; they refill by reading the table. Saying nothing is the correct local move.

Climb the south tower of the Cathedral. The 533 spiral steps to the top take about 20 minutes and reward you with the only panoramic view in Cologne where you can see all the way to the Belgian Ardennes on a clear day. The Cathedral from outside is famous; from above the city it is something else entirely.

Visit Kolumba on a quiet weekday morning. Peter Zumthor designed the museum’s narrow slit windows to shift the quality of light across the Roman ruins in the basement throughout the day. The excavated foundation looks completely different at 10am than at 4pm — most visitors see one and not the other.

Eat at the Alter Markt on a weekday lunchtime. The square between Gross St. Martin and the Town Hall fills with locals when the tourist restaurants are at capacity — the food is identical at a fraction of the wait.
